```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dev = "png",
                      fig.retina = 2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5,
                      fig.align = "center")
library(mlvtoolbox)
```

`mlvtoolbox` measures the geometry of line drawings: the orientation, length
and curvature of each contour, the junctions where contours meet, and the
medial-axis symmetry of the spaces between them. This vignette builds a small
drawing by hand, measures it, and turns the measurements into the histograms
and per-contour feature tables used as predictors in behavioural and
neuroimaging analyses. Every number quoted below is computed when the vignette
is built, and each is small enough to check by hand.

```{r showcase-scene, include = FALSE}
# A synthetic room: a wall corner, a window with mullions and a curtain, a
# picture, a table, a hanging lamp and a box, as 17 contours.
sc_line <- function(x, y) { n <- length(x); cbind(x1 = x[-n], y1 = y[-n], x2 = x[-1], y2 = y[-1]) }
sc_closed <- function(x, y) sc_line(c(x, x[1]), c(y, y[1]))
curtain_y <- seq(25, 85, by = 2.5); bulb_t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 25)
scene <- mlv_drawing(list(
  corner = sc_line(c(120, 120), c(5, 105)),
  floor_left = sc_line(c(120, 5), c(105, 140)),
  floor_right = sc_line(c(120, 235), c(105, 140)),
  window = sc_closed(c(30, 80, 80, 30), c(40, 30, 70, 80)),
  mullion_v = sc_line(c(55, 55), c(35, 75)),
  mullion_h = sc_line(c(30, 80), c(60, 50)),
  curtain = sc_line(91 + 3 * sin(curtain_y / 5), curtain_y),
  picture = sc_closed(c(198, 228, 228, 198), c(40, 46, 76, 82)),
  table_top = sc_line(c(140, 205), c(135, 135)),
  leg_left = sc_line(c(150, 150), c(135, 155)),
  leg_right = sc_line(c(195, 195), c(135, 155)),
  cord = sc_line(c(165, 165), c(5, 40)),
  shade = sc_line(c(150, 165, 180), c(52, 40, 52)),
  bulb = sc_line(165 + 6 * cos(bulb_t), 60 - 6 * sin(bulb_t)),
  box_left = sc_line(c(60, 42), c(128, 135)),
  box_right = sc_line(c(60, 78), c(128, 135)),
  box_front = sc_line(c(60, 60), c(128, 148))),
  width = 240, height = 160)
scene_junctions <- detect_junctions(scene)
scene_mat <- analyse_mat(scene, properties = "parallelism")
stopifnot(all(c("T", "Y", "X", "Arrow") %in% scene_junctions$type))

# Drawing helpers for the figure. The phone-width copy of a figure is a replay
# of the desktop drawing, so anything measured from the device is drawn
# through recordGraphics(), which re-evaluates it on replay.
replay <- function(f, ...) {
  args <- list(...)
  recordGraphics(do.call(f, args), list(f = f, args = args), globalenv())
}
panel <- function(title, tag) {
  title(main = title, cex.main = 1, font.main = 1, line = 1.15)
  mtext(tag, side = 3, line = 0.2, cex = 0.7, col = "grey40")
}
# Junction types: Okabe-Ito colours this page does not give to contours.
type_cols <- c(T = "black", Y = "#56B4E9", X = "#CC79A7", Arrow = "#F0E442")
type_text <- c(T = "white", Y = "black", X = "black", Arrow = "black")
type_letter <- c(T = "T", Y = "Y", X = "X", Arrow = "A")
# Coloured badges with the type's letter, as in the key; smaller on a narrow
# device, where the window's five junctions sit close together.
badges <- function(j) replay(function(x, y, type) {
  s <- if (par("din")[1] < 5) 0.6 else 1
  points(x, y, pch = 21, bg = type_cols[type], col = "grey20", cex = 1.9 * s, lwd = 0.6)
  text(x, y, type_letter[type], cex = 0.6 * s, font = 2, col = type_text[type])
}, x = j$x, y = j$y, type = j$type)
type_key <- function(j) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); plot.new()
  n <- table(factor(j$type, levels = names(type_cols)))
  at <- seq(0.14, 0.86, length.out = length(n))
  points(at, rep(0.55, length(n)), pch = 21, bg = type_cols, col = "grey20", cex = 1.9, lwd = 0.6)
  text(at, 0.55, type_letter, cex = 0.6, font = 2, col = type_text)
  text(at, 0.12, sprintf("%s %d", names(n), as.integer(n)), cex = 0.75)
  par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 2.2, 0.2))
}
axis_key <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); plot.new()
  segments(0.12, 0.5, 0.2, 0.5, col = axis_col, lwd = 2.5)
  text(0.22, 0.5, "medial axis", adj = 0, cex = 0.75)
  symbols(0.6, 0.5, circles = 0.03, inches = FALSE, add = TRUE, fg = "grey55", lwd = 0.8)
  text(0.65, 0.5, "inscribed disc", adj = 0, cex = 0.75)
  par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 2.2, 0.2))
}
# The medial axis in the package's one encoding: red, thinner than the ink.
axis_col <- eval(formals(draw_mat_axis)$col, environment(draw_mat_axis))
# A handful of inscribed discs, at the axis points nearest to chosen spots: a
# window pane, the wall, the floor, under the table, by the lamp, the picture.
axis_points <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scene_mat$mat$branches, function(b) b[, c("x", "y", "radius")]))
spots <- rbind(c(42, 47), c(103, 55), c(100, 128), c(172, 147), c(140, 28), c(213, 61))
disc_points <- axis_points[apply(spots, 1, function(p)
  which.min((axis_points$x - p[1])^2 + (axis_points$y - p[2])^2)), ]
disc_points <- disc_points[with(disc_points, x - radius > 0.5 & x + radius < 240.5 &
                                  y - radius > 0.5 & y + radius < 160.5), ]
# Mapped scores drawn `widen` pixels to each side of the ink, so their colour
# can be read at a glance. Ink pixels keep their own scores; each added pixel
# takes the score of its nearest ink pixel.
widen <- 1
mapped_wide <- function(d, property, w) {
  img <- d$mat_images[[property]]; out <- img
  steps <- expand.grid(dr = -w:w, dc = -w:w)
  steps <- steps[order(steps$dr^2 + steps$dc^2), ][-1, ]
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(steps))) {
    dr <- steps$dr[k]; dc <- steps$dc[k]
    shifted <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(img), ncol(img))
    rr <- max(1, 1 + dr):min(nrow(img), nrow(img) + dr)
    cc <- max(1, 1 + dc):min(ncol(img), ncol(img) + dc)
    shifted[rr, cc] <- img[rr - dr, cc - dc]
    fill <- !is.finite(out) & is.finite(shifted)
    out[fill] <- shifted[fill]
  }
  fill <- matrix("transparent", nrow(out), ncol(out)); ok <- is.finite(out)
  pal <- grDevices::hcl.colors(256, "Viridis")
  fill[ok] <- pal[1 + pmin(255, floor(out[ok] * 256))]
  rasterImage(as.raster(fill), 0.5, nrow(out) + 0.5, ncol(out) + 0.5, 0.5, interpolate = FALSE)
}
```

```{r fig-showcase, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6.9, fig.cap = sprintf("What the package measures, on one synthetic room of %d contours. Top: the %d junctions it finds, coloured by type, and segment orientation. Bottom: the medial axis (red) between the contours, with %d of its inscribed discs, and the parallelism of the space beside each contour, mapped back onto it (drawn %d px wide; added pixels copy the nearest ink pixel). Each panel names its vignette.", length(scene$contours), nrow(scene_junctions), nrow(disc_points), 2 * widen + 1)}
layout(matrix(1:8, 4), heights = c(1, lcm(1.25), 1, lcm(1.25)))
op <- par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 2.2, 0.2), cex = 0.8)
# Column 1: junctions, then the medial axis.
plot(scene, lwd = 1.2, axes = FALSE, frame = FALSE)
panel("Junctions", "vignette(\"junctions\")")
badges(scene_junctions)
type_key(scene_junctions)
plot(scene, lwd = 1.2, axes = FALSE, frame = FALSE)
panel("Medial axis", "vignette(\"medial-axis\")")
for (k in seq_len(nrow(disc_points)))
  symbols(disc_points$x[k], disc_points$y[k], circles = disc_points$radius[k],
          inches = FALSE, add = TRUE, fg = "grey55", lwd = 0.8)
draw_mat_axis(scene_mat$mat, width = 0.9)
axis_key()
# Column 2: orientation, then parallelism mapped onto the contours.
plot(scene, property = "orientation", lwd = 2, axes = FALSE, frame = FALSE, legend = FALSE)
panel("Orientation", "vignette(\"getting-started\")")
colour_key(scene, "orientation", cex = 0.7)
plot(scene, col = NA, axes = FALSE, frame = FALSE)
panel("Parallelism on the contours", "vignette(\"medial-axis\")")
mapped_wide(scene_mat$drawing, "parallelism", widen)
colour_key(scene_mat$drawing, "parallelism", cex = 0.7)
par(op)
layout(1)
```

The code for this scene and figure is in the appendix at the end of this
vignette; the sections below build up each measure on a smaller drawing.

## A drawing is a list of contours

A *contour* is one continuous stroke, stored as a matrix with one row per
straight *segment* and columns `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`. The end of each row is
the start of the next, so the rows trace the stroke in order; the shared
points are the contour's *vertices*. A drawing (`mlv_drawing`) is a list of
contours plus the size of the canvas in pixels.

Coordinates are image coordinates: x increases to the right, y increases
downward, and pixel centres sit at integers, starting at (1, 1). Coordinates
need not be integers, and a contour may extend past the canvas.

The drawing below has four contours: a straight horizon, a roof whose two
slopes meet at a 90 degree apex, a sampled sine wave, and a closed 32-sided
polygon approximating a circle (the sun). A closed contour is one whose last
point equals its first.

```{r drawing}
polyline <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  cbind(x1 = x[-n], y1 = y[-n], x2 = x[-1], y2 = y[-1])
}
wave_x <- seq(65, 115, by = 2.5)
sun_t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 33)

drawing <- mlv_drawing(
  list(horizon = polyline(c(5, 115), c(60, 60)),
       roof    = polyline(c(15, 35, 55), c(60, 40, 60)),
       wave    = polyline(wave_x, 25 + 6 * sin(wave_x / 5)),
       sun     = polyline(90 + 10 * cos(sun_t), 45 - 10 * sin(sun_t))),
  width = 120, height = 80,
  ids = c("horizon", "roof", "wave", "sun"))
drawing
```

```{r label-helper, include = FALSE}
# The phone-width copy of each figure is a replay of the desktop drawing, so
# anything measured from the device (text widths, inches) is drawn through
# recordGraphics(), which re-evaluates it on replay.
replay <- function(f, ...) {
  args <- list(...)
  recordGraphics(do.call(f, args), list(f = f, args = args), globalenv())
}
# One Okabe-Ito colour per contour, shared by the drawing's labels and the
# stacked histograms below.
contour_cols <- c(horizon = "#0072B2", roof = "#D55E00", wave = "#009E73", sun = "#E69F00")
label_contours <- function() replay(function(cols) {
  x <- c(110, 22, 90, 107); y <- c(56, 46, 15, 36)
  text(x, y, names(cols), cex = 0.8, col = "grey20")
  w <- strwidth(names(cols), cex = 0.8); gap <- 1.1 * strwidth("m", cex = 0.8)
  points(x - w / 2 - gap, y, pch = 15, cex = 0.9, col = cols)
}, cols = contour_cols)
# Axis titles just outside the canvas edges, wherever asp = 1 puts them.
canvas_titles <- function(d, xlab, ylab) replay(function(w, h, xlab, ylab) {
  line <- par("csi") * diff(par("usr")[1:2]) / par("pin")[1]
  text((w + 1) / 2, h + 0.5 + 2.1 * line, xlab, xpd = NA, cex = 0.85, col = "grey30")
  text(0.5 - 2.6 * line, (h + 1) / 2, ylab, srt = 90, xpd = NA, cex = 0.85, col = "grey30")
}, w = d$width, h = d$height, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab)
# A key in one centred row, a swatch and a name per contour, filling a strip.
contour_legend <- function() {
  plot.new()
  replay(function(cols) {
    ids <- names(cols); gap <- strwidth("m", cex = 0.85)
    w <- strwidth(ids, cex = 0.85) + 3.2 * gap
    x0 <- 0.5 - sum(w) / 2 + c(0, cumsum(w)[-length(w)])
    points(x0, rep(0.5, length(ids)), pch = 15, cex = 1.3, col = cols)
    text(x0 + gap, 0.5, ids, adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 0.85)
  }, cols = contour_cols)
}
# A short line at each orientation, drawn under the bars at x = at.
orientation_glyphs <- function(at, degrees) replay(function(at, degrees) {
  upi <- diff(par("usr")[1:2]) / par("pin")[1]; vpi <- diff(par("usr")[3:4]) / par("pin")[2]
  g <- min(0.09, 0.33 * diff(at[1:2]) / upi); a <- degrees * pi / 180; y <- -0.17 * vpi
  segments(at - g * upi * cos(a), y - g * vpi * sin(a), at + g * upi * cos(a),
           y + g * vpi * sin(a), xpd = NA, lwd = 1.2, col = "grey20")
  show <- degrees %% 45 == 0
  text(at[show], y - 0.2 * vpi, paste0(degrees[show], "°"), xpd = NA, cex = 0.75)
}, at = at, degrees = degrees)
```
```{r fig-drawing, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = sprintf("The drawing on its %d × %d pixel canvas. The y axis points down, as in an image, and dots mark the vertices: the horizon has %d, the roof %d and the sun %d. The roof's vertices are labelled, for the hand calculations below; the coloured squares key each contour to the histograms further down.", drawing$width, drawing$height, nrow(drawing$contours[[1]]) + 1L, nrow(drawing$contours[[2]]) + 1L, nrow(drawing$contours[[4]]))}
op <- par(mar = c(3, 3.2, 0.3, 0.5))
plot(drawing, lwd = 1.5, frame = FALSE)
canvas_titles(drawing, "x (px)", "y (px), pointing down")
vertices <- do.call(rbind, lapply(drawing$contours, function(z) z[, 1:2]))
points(vertices, pch = 16, cex = 0.35)
roof_xy <- rbind(drawing$contours[[2]][, 1:2], drawing$contours[[2]][2, 3:4])
text(roof_xy[, 1], roof_xy[, 2], sprintf("(%g, %g)", roof_xy[, 1], roof_xy[, 2]),
     pos = c(1, 3, 1), cex = 0.7, col = "grey30", offset = 0.4)
label_contours()
par(op)
```
`mlv_drawing()` checks the input before anything is measured. Rows of a
contour must connect, and a segment of zero length is an error unless you ask
for it to be removed with `zero_length = "drop"`. Keep strokes that a viewer
sees as separate in separate contours: contour identity determines which
crossings count as junctions and which histogram a contour's length enters.

## Segment measurements

`as.data.frame()` returns one row per segment with three measurements.

- **Orientation** is the direction from the segment's start to its end, in
  degrees counterclockwise from the rightward x axis. Because y points down,
  "counterclockwise" means as seen on the screen: a segment drawn up and to
  the right has orientation 45. Orientation is directed (0 to 360); histograms
  treat it as axial, modulo 180, because a line has no direction.
- **Length** is the Euclidean length in pixels.
- **Curvature** is in degrees per pixel. A polygon turns only at its
  vertices, so curvature is defined by where each vertex's turning angle is
  placed. The default *vertex turning* estimator spreads each turn evenly over
  the vertex's *dual cell*, which runs from the midpoint of the segment before
  the vertex to the midpoint of the segment after it, so every turn is counted
  once. A segment's curvature is its mean curvature: the turning that falls
  on the segment divided by its length. The two end halves of an open contour
  belong to no vertex and carry no turning.

```{r segments}
segments <- as.data.frame(drawing)
segments[segments$contour_id %in% c("horizon", "roof"),
         c("contour_id", "segment_index", "length", "orientation", "curvature")]
```

```{r roof-check, include = FALSE}
roof <- segments[segments$contour_id == "roof", ]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(roof$orientation, c(45, 315))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(roof$length, rep(sqrt(800), 2))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(roof$curvature, rep(45 / sqrt(800), 2))))
sun <- segments[segments$contour_id == "sun", ]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sun$curvature, rep(11.25 / sun$length[1], nrow(sun)))))
roof_profile <- curvature_profile(subset_contours(drawing, "roof"), "turning")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(roof_profile$curvature, c(0, 90, 90, 0) / sqrt(800))))
circle_curvature <- 180 / (pi * 10)
```

These values can be checked by hand. The left slope of the roof runs from
(15, 60) to (35, 40): 20 pixels right and 20 pixels up the screen, so its
orientation is 45 degrees and its length is √800 =
`r round(roof$length[1], 2)` pixels. The right slope runs down and to the
right, orientation 315. At the apex the direction changes by 90 degrees. The
apex's dual cell is the inner half of each slope, √800 pixels in all, so
each slope receives 45 degrees of turning and a mean curvature of
45 / `r round(roof$length[1], 2)` = `r round(roof$curvature[1], 2)` degrees
per pixel. The roof's length-weighted total curvature is
`r round(sum(roof$curvature * roof$length), 1)` degrees, the single turn at
the apex. The sun's 32 vertices each turn by 360 / 32 = 11.25 degrees; each
side, `r round(sun$length[1], 3)` pixels long, receives half of the turn at
each of its ends, a curvature of `r round(sun$curvature[1], 2)` degrees per
pixel. A true circle of radius 10 has curvature 180 / (10π) =
`r round(circle_curvature, 2)` degrees per pixel.

Within a segment the curvature is not uniform: the density is
`r round(roof_profile$curvature[2], 2)` degrees per pixel on the roof's two
inner halves and zero on its outer halves. `curvature_profile()` returns
this piecewise density, one row per piece, and the curvature histograms
below integrate it exactly.

The published MLV estimator, `estimator = "mlv2023"`, is available for
comparison with published values. It returns one row per segment and gives
each segment the whole turn to the next segment divided by its own length;
the last segment of an open contour, which has no next segment, repeats the
turn from the one before it.

```{r segments-mlv2023}
published <- as.data.frame(drawing, estimator = "mlv2023")
published_roof <- published[published$contour_id == "roof", ]
published_roof[, c("segment_index", "length", "orientation", "curvature")]
```

```{r published-check, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(published_roof$curvature, rep(90 / sqrt(800), 2))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(sum(published_roof$curvature * published_roof$length), 180)))
```

Both slopes now receive `r round(published_roof$curvature[1], 2)` degrees
per pixel, the whole 90 degree turn each, so the roof's total curvature is
`r round(sum(published_roof$curvature * published_roof$length), 1)` degrees,
twice the actual turn. Because a vertex's turn is divided by the length of
one neighbouring segment only, the published values also depend on how a
curve is sampled: a circle whose vertices alternate between short and long
spacings receives two different curvatures, where the turning estimator
gives one. The section on feature specifications below compares the
estimators.

`plot()` colours segments by a measurement and adds a colour bar that names
the quantity and its unit. Orientation uses a cyclic palette over 0 to 180
degrees, so the roof's two slopes (45 and 135 degrees, axially) sit on opposite
sides of the colour wheel and a horizontal segment has the same colour
whichever way it was drawn. Length and curvature use a sequential palette.
In the figure below each panel is drawn with `legend = FALSE` and its key by
`colour_key()` in a layout cell of its own, which keeps the key off the
drawing; `colour_key()` also lets several panels share one key.

```{r fig-properties, fig.height = 2.7, fig.cap = sprintf("Each segment coloured by its orientation (left) and by its mean curvature (right). The orientation palette wraps, so 0° and 180° share a colour, and the roof's slopes, at 45° and 135°, sit on opposite sides of the key. The straight horizon has zero curvature, the roof's two slopes share the apex turn equally (%.2f°/px each), and the wave curves most at its peaks and troughs.", roof$curvature[1])}
# The keys name the quantities, so the panels need no titles.
layout(matrix(1:4, 2), heights = c(1, lcm(2.4)))
op <- par(mar = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3))
# Crop to the ink, which fills the canvas only between rows 15 and 60.
window <- list(xlim = c(1, 120), ylim = c(65, 13))
plot(drawing, property = "orientation", lwd = 2.5, axes = FALSE, legend = FALSE,
     frame = FALSE, xlim = window$xlim, ylim = window$ylim)
colour_key(drawing, "orientation", glyphs = TRUE)
plot(drawing, property = "curvature", lwd = 2.5, axes = FALSE, legend = FALSE,
     frame = FALSE, xlim = window$xlim, ylim = window$ylim)
# The roof's slopes carry the same value; label it on each.
text(c(25, 45), c(49, 49), sprintf("%.2f", roof$curvature), pos = c(2, 4), cex = 0.7,
     col = "grey25")
colour_key(drawing, "curvature")
par(op)
layout(1)
```
The colour scale for length and curvature runs over the data range by
default. Pass a fixed `zlim` when several drawings must share one scale.

## Storing measurements and junctions

`compute_contour_properties()` measures the drawing once and stores the
results on it: the segment table, the length of each contour, and the
junctions between contours.

```{r compute}
measured <- compute_contour_properties(drawing)
measured$contour_properties
measured$junctions[, c("x", "y", "type", "min_angle", "max_angle")]
```

```{r junction-check, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(nrow(measured$junctions) == 2L,
          all(measured$junctions$type == "T"))
```

The roof ends on the horizon at both eaves, so the drawing has
`r nrow(measured$junctions)` junctions, both T-junctions: the horizon
contributes two arms and the roof slope a third, at
`r round(measured$junctions$min_angle[1])` degrees to the horizon. How
junctions are found, what an arm is and how the type and angles are defined
are the subject of `vignette("junctions", package = "mlvtoolbox")`.

## Histograms

Most analyses do not use segment tables directly. They use histograms that
summarize a drawing, or each contour, in a fixed set of bins.
`contour_statistics()` returns them in long form, one row per bin.

```{r statistics}
stats <- contour_statistics(measured,
                            properties = c("orientation", "length", "curvature"))
head(stats[stats$property == "orientation",
           c("property", "label", "lower", "upper", "value", "units")], 8)
```

```{r orientation-numbers, include = FALSE}
ori <- stats[stats$property == "orientation", ]
len <- stats[stats$property == "length", ]
crv <- stats[stats$property == "curvature", ]
length_edges <- c(len$lower, len$upper[nrow(len)])
curvature_edges <- c(crv$lower, crv$upper[nrow(crv)])
by_contour <- contour_statistics(measured, properties = "orientation", by = "contour")
in_bin <- function(id, label) by_contour$value[by_contour$contour_id == id & by_contour$label == label]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(in_bin("roof", "45"), sqrt(800))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(in_bin("roof", "135"), sqrt(800))))
horizon_bin <- len[len$lower <= 110 & len$upper > 110, ]
other_lengths <- measured$contour_properties$length[-1]
below <- len[which(len$bin == horizon_bin$bin - 1L), ]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(horizon_bin$value, 110)),
          all(other_lengths >= below$lower & other_lengths < below$upper))
```

The weighting is part of the definition of each histogram, and the defaults
were chosen so that the histograms describe ink, not vertex counts:

- the orientation histogram adds each segment's length to the bin of its axial
  orientation, so a contour sampled with more vertices does not count more;
- the length histogram adds each whole contour's length to the bin of that
  length;
- the curvature histogram adds length to the bin of the curvature density
  along it, so the roof's inner halves enter one bin and its outer halves the
  zero bin.

Length and curvature bins are equally spaced in log10(1 + x) between the ends
of `length_range` (by default 2 pixels and the canvas width plus height) and
`curvature_range` (by default 0 to 90 degrees per pixel). Here the 8 length
bins have
edges at `r paste(signif(length_edges, 3), collapse = ", ")` pixels, and the
curvature bins at `r paste(signif(curvature_edges, 3), collapse = ", ")`
degrees per pixel. Values outside a range enter the first or last bin.

Orientation bins are centred on 0, 22.5, 45, … degrees, so the first bin runs
from −11.25 to 11.25 degrees. It holds `r round(ori$value[1], 1)` pixels: the
110-pixel horizon plus the near-horizontal parts of the wave and the sun. The
45 degree bin receives the left roof slope (`r round(in_bin("roof", "45"), 1)`
pixels) and about as much again from the rising flanks of the wave
(`r round(in_bin("wave", "45"), 1)` pixels), plus
`r round(in_bin("sun", "45"), 1)` from the sun. The 135 degree bin receives
the right slope, `r round(in_bin("wave", "135"), 1)` pixels of wave and the
same `r round(in_bin("sun", "135"), 1)` from the sun. In the length
histogram the horizon alone fills the bin from
`r round(horizon_bin$lower, 1)` to `r round(horizon_bin$upper, 1)` pixels;
the other three contours, `r round(min(other_lengths))` to
`r round(max(other_lengths))` pixels long, share the bin below it.

```{r fig-histograms, fig.height = 3.4, fig.cap = sprintf("Histograms for the whole drawing, each bar split by contour. Left: segment length per orientation bin; the horizontal bin dominates, with %.1f px of ink. Right: whole-contour length per length bin, drawn at the bins' true widths on a log10(1 + length) axis; the horizon alone fills one bin, and the other three contours share the next shorter bin.", ori$value[1])}
ids <- names(contour_cols)
len_by_contour <- contour_statistics(measured, properties = "length", by = "contour")
per_contour <- function(tab, bins) t(sapply(ids, function(id)
  vapply(bins, function(b) sum(tab$value[tab$contour_id == id & tab$bin == b]), 0)))
ori_stack <- per_contour(by_contour, ori$bin); len_stack <- per_contour(len_by_contour, len$bin)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(colSums(ori_stack)), ori$value)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(unname(colSums(len_stack)), len$value)))
layout(matrix(c(1, 1, 2, 3), 2, byrow = TRUE), heights = c(lcm(0.9), 1))
op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8, cex.main = 1, font.main = 1)
contour_legend()
par(mar = c(3.6, 4, 1.6, 0.8))
top <- max(pretty(c(0, ori$value)))
mids <- barplot(ori_stack, col = contour_cols, border = "white", lwd = 0.5, space = 0.15,
                ylim = c(0, top), axes = FALSE, names.arg = rep("", ncol(ori_stack)),
                main = "Orientation")
axis(2, at = pretty(c(0, top)), col = "grey55", col.ticks = "grey55", tcl = -0.3)
title(ylab = "segment length (px)", line = 2.6, cex.lab = 0.85)
# A line under each bar shows the bin's orientation.
orientation_glyphs(mids, ori$center)
# Length bins are equal in log10(1 + x); draw them at their true widths.
tx <- function(v) log10(1 + v)
top <- max(pretty(c(0, len$value)))
plot(NA, xlim = tx(range(length_edges)), ylim = c(0, top), axes = FALSE, xaxs = "i",
     yaxs = "i", xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "Length")
abline(v = tx(length_edges), col = "grey90", lwd = 0.8)
base <- 0
for (k in seq_along(ids)) {
  h <- len_stack[k, ]
  rect(tx(len$lower), base, tx(len$upper), base + h, col = contour_cols[k],
       border = ifelse(h > 0, "white", NA), lwd = 0.5)
  base <- base + h
}
axis(1, at = tx(c(2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200)), labels = FALSE, col = "grey55",
     col.ticks = "grey55", tcl = -0.3)
axis(1, at = tx(c(2, 10, 50, 200)), labels = c(2, 10, 50, 200), lwd = 0, mgp = c(3, 0.5, 0))
axis(2, at = pretty(c(0, top)), col = "grey55", col.ticks = "grey55", tcl = -0.3)
title(ylab = "summed contour length (px)", line = 2.6, cex.lab = 0.85)
mtext("length (px)", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.7, col = "grey30")
par(op)
layout(1)
```
With `normalize = TRUE` each histogram is divided by total contour length and
expressed per 10,000 pixels of contour, so drawings with different amounts of
ink can be compared. With `by = "contour"` the histograms are computed per
contour instead of per drawing.

## Per-contour feature tables

`feature_table()` puts the per-contour histograms side by side: one row per
contour, one column per bin, normalized per 10,000 pixels by default. This is
the format used to fit a model of a per-contour response.

```{r features}
features <- feature_table(measured)
dim(features)
features[, c("contour_id", paste0("orientation_", 1:8))]
```

```{r feature-check, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(features$orientation_1[1], 10000)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(unlist(features[4, paste0("orientation_", 1:8)],
                                  use.names = FALSE), rep(1250, 8))))
```

The rows can again be read off the geometry. All of the horizon's length lies
in the first orientation bin, so it scores
`r format(features$orientation_1[1], big.mark = ",")` there
and zero elsewhere. The roof's length divides equally between the 45 and 135
degree bins (`r format(features$orientation_3[2], big.mark = ",")` each). The sun's 32 equal segments
step through every orientation in 11.25 degree increments, four per bin, so
each of the eight bins holds `r format(features$orientation_1[4], big.mark = ",")`.

The table carries a schema that records each column's bin edges, weights,
units and normalization. `feature_schema(features)` returns it, and model
prediction uses it to refuse tables measured differently from the training
data (see `vignette("workflows", package = "mlvtoolbox")`).

## Feature specifications

Two settings above depend on things other than the contour geometry. The
default length bins end at the canvas width plus height, so the same contours
on a larger canvas fall into different bins. The curvature estimator, junction
rule and medial-axis method also change the numbers. A *feature
specification* fixes all of these in one object, so that every drawing in a
study is measured the same way and the choices are recorded with the results.

```{r canvas-dependence}
larger <- mlv_drawing(drawing$contours, width = 240, height = 160,
                      ids = drawing$ids)
default_small <- feature_table(drawing, properties = "length")
default_large <- feature_table(larger, properties = "length")
rbind(small_canvas = default_small[1, -1], large_canvas = default_large[1, -1])
```

```{r spec}
spec <- feature_spec(c("orientation", "length", "curvature"),
                     length_range = c(2, 400))
identical(feature_table(drawing, spec = spec)[, -1],
          feature_table(larger, spec = spec)[, -1])
spec$settings[c("estimator", "bins", "length_range", "normalize")]
```

```{r spec-check, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(feature_table(drawing, spec = spec)[, -1],
                    feature_table(larger, spec = spec)[, -1]))
```

Under the specification the horizon's length bin no longer depends on the
canvas. The specification also records method definitions for the curvature
estimator, the junction rule and the medial-axis stages, which is why a table
built under one specification cannot silently be mixed with one built under
another.

The `estimator` setting selects the curvature definition. `"turning"`, the
default, is the vertex turning estimator described above: each vertex turn
is counted once, spread evenly over the vertex's dual cell, and it has no
tuning parameter. `"arclength"` spreads each turn over
a tent of half-width `curvature_scale` pixels along the contour, so curvature
is expressed at a stated spatial scale and each turn is still counted once.
Its values stop depending on vertex density once segments are shorter than
that scale; a coarsely sampled contour still concentrates its turns at its
few vertices. Both wrap around closed contours. `"mlv2023"` is the published
estimator.

```{r estimators}
roof_only <- subset_contours(drawing, "roof")
arc_scale <- 2  # half-width, in pixels, of the arc-length estimator's tent
profiles <- list(mlv2023 = as.data.frame(roof_only, estimator = "mlv2023"),
                 turning = curvature_profile(roof_only, "turning"),
                 arclength = curvature_profile(roof_only, "arclength", scale = arc_scale))
sapply(profiles, function(p) sum(p$curvature * p$length))
```

```{r estimator-check, include = FALSE}
totals <- sapply(profiles, function(p) sum(p$curvature * p$length))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(totals), c(180, 90, 90))))
```

The integrated curvature of the roof, the sum of curvature times length, is
`r totals[["mlv2023"]]` degrees under the published estimator and
`r totals[["turning"]]` degrees under the turning and arc-length estimators, which matches
the single 90 degree turn at the apex. `contour_turning()` lists the
unsmoothed vertex turns directly.

```{r fig-estimators, fig.height = 3.4, fig.cap = sprintf("Turning accumulated along the roof by three estimators; each curve's final height is the total turning it assigns. The published estimator (mlv2023; grey, since this page's hues name contours) spreads the apex turn over both whole slopes and counts it twice, reaching %g°; the turning estimator spreads it over the slopes' inner halves and the arc-length estimator %g px either side of the apex, and both reach the %g° turn.", totals[["mlv2023"]], arc_scale, totals[["turning"]])}
# Exact running integral of a piecewise-linear curvature profile.
cumulative <- function(p, n = 40) {
  s0 <- if (is.null(p$s_start)) c(0, cumsum(p$length)[-nrow(p)]) else p$s_start
  s1 <- if (is.null(p$s_end)) cumsum(p$length) else p$s_end
  k0 <- if (is.null(p$curvature_start)) p$curvature else p$curvature_start
  k1 <- if (is.null(p$curvature_end)) p$curvature else p$curvature_end
  s <- 0; total <- 0; out <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(s0)) {
    t <- seq(0, s1[i] - s0[i], length.out = n)
    run <- total + k0[i] * t + (k1[i] - k0[i]) / (2 * (s1[i] - s0[i])) * t^2
    s <- c(s, s0[i] + t[-1]); out <- c(out, run[-1]); total <- run[n]
  }
  list(s = s, turn = out)
}
curves <- lapply(profiles, cumulative)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(vapply(curves, function(z) z$turn[length(z$turn)], 0),
                           totals)))
# Three estimators of one roof: line weights and types, not hues (the hues of
# this page belong to the four contours).
est_style <- list(mlv2023 = list(col = "grey60", lwd = 3.2, lty = 1),
                  turning = list(col = "black", lwd = 1.8, lty = 1),
                  arclength = list(col = "black", lwd = 1.8, lty = 2))
apex <- sqrt(800); roof_length <- 2 * apex
op <- par(mar = c(3.4, 3.8, 0.6, 2.6), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, roof_length), ylim = c(0, 190), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(h = c(90, 180), col = "grey90", lwd = 0.8)
abline(v = apex, lty = 3, col = "grey40")
for (e in c("mlv2023", "arclength", "turning"))
  lines(curves[[e]]$s, curves[[e]]$turn, lwd = est_style[[e]]$lwd,
        col = est_style[[e]]$col, lty = est_style[[e]]$lty)
axis(1, at = c(seq(0, 50, by = 10), roof_length),
     labels = c(seq(0, 50, by = 10), round(roof_length, 1)), col = "grey55",
     col.ticks = "grey55", tcl = -0.3, mgp = c(3, 0.5, 0))
axis(2, at = c(0, 45, 90, 135, 180), col = "grey55", col.ticks = "grey55", tcl = -0.3)
title(xlab = "arc length along the roof (px)", line = 2, cex.lab = 0.85)
title(ylab = "accumulated turning (°)", line = 2.6, cex.lab = 0.85)
text(apex, 186, "apex", pos = 4, cex = 0.75, col = "grey30", offset = 0.3)
# Names against each curve, where it is alone; totals at the right-hand ends.
text(26.6, 98, "published\n(mlv2023)", adj = c(1, 0), cex = 0.8)
text(37, 62, "turning", adj = c(0, 1), cex = 0.8)
text(29.6, 25, "arc length", adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 0.8)
text(roof_length, unique(totals), paste0(unique(totals), "°"), pos = 4, xpd = NA, cex = 0.8,
     offset = 0.3)
par(op)
```
The estimators also differ in how they respond to sampling. A circle of
radius 10 drawn as a regular polygon has one curvature under every estimator,
the polygon's turn over its side, which approaches 180 / (10π) degrees per
pixel as vertices are added. If the vertices instead alternate between a
short and a long spacing (1 : 2 in angle), the turning estimator still gives
a single value, while the published estimator divides each vertex's turn by
the length of the segment before it and splits the circle into two
curvatures:

```{r resampling}
circle <- function(n, spacing) {
  t <- c(0, cumsum(rep(spacing, length.out = n))) / sum(rep(spacing, length.out = n)) * 2 * pi
  mlv_drawing(list(polyline(60 + 10 * cos(t), 40 - 10 * sin(t))), 120, 80)
}
occupied <- function(d, e) {
  h <- contour_statistics(d, "curvature", estimator = e)
  paste(sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", h$lower, h$upper)[h$value > 0], collapse = " and ")
}
resampled <- expand.grid(vertices = c(16, 32, 64, 128), estimator = c("turning", "mlv2023"),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
resampled$regular <- mapply(function(n, e) occupied(circle(n, 1), e), resampled$vertices, resampled$estimator)
resampled$alternating <- mapply(function(n, e) occupied(circle(n, c(1, 2)), e), resampled$vertices, resampled$estimator)
resampled
```

```{r resampling-check, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(length(unique(resampled$regular)) == 1L,
          all(resampled$alternating[resampled$estimator == "turning"] == resampled$regular[1]),
          all(grepl(" and ", resampled$alternating[resampled$estimator == "mlv2023"])))
```

The table gives the range, in degrees per pixel, of each curvature bin that
receives length (8 bins from 0 to 90 degrees per pixel). For new studies use the turning default,
or the arc-length estimator with a curvature scale chosen for the stimulus
resolution when curvature should be stated at a spatial scale; choose a scale
longer than the typical segment so that the values do not depend on how finely
contours were sampled. The published estimator is the right choice only when
results must be comparable with published MLV values
(`vignette("mlv-compatibility", package = "mlvtoolbox")`). The same
specification can express physical units: `units = "visual_degrees"` with a
`pixels_per_degree` calibration reports lengths in degrees of visual angle
(curvature stays in geometric degrees per unit length).
